# Decision 0001: work items stay the tracker, and GitHub issues mirror them one way

**Date:** 2026-10-24
**Decided by:** the repository owner (2026-10-24); recorded by spec-author

## The call

The `**/.issue/<id>-<slug>.yml` work items stay the tracker and the record of
truth. GitHub issues become a one-way, read-only mirror of them and of the
epics under `epics/`: written from `main` on every push that changes them,
never read back into an item. `github_mode` stays `false`.

### Agreed design

The owner approved this design with the call. `0055-F9` claims sourced to the
owner cite this list.

1. One issue per work item and one per epic (`epics/*/epic.md`).
2. Each issue is identified by a hidden marker in its body,
   `<!-- specht-item: <id> -->`, and carries the label `mirrored`.
3. An item's issue is titled `<id>: <title>`; an epic's `Epic <id>: <title>`.
4. Labels derived from the item: `type:<type>`, `status:<status>` (none for
   `done`), and `goal` for an id listed in `.issue/.goal`. The mirror creates
   the labels it needs.
5. An item `done` has its issue closed as completed; any other status has it
   open, reopened if closed.
6. `parent:` is a sub-issue link; a Feature item whose parent is an epic hangs
   under the epic's issue.
7. The body carries the marker; a provenance line naming the item's
   repository-relative path on `main`; for a done item a "Delivered by" line
   derived from git history on each run (the squash subject naming the item,
   else the commit that set it `done`, else that commit's sha - this order
   is superseded by decision 0009); the rendered
   summary, acceptance criteria, decisions and out-of-scope entries; the item
   verbatim in a fenced yaml block; and a footer saying the issue is a
   read-only mirror whose comments are not read.
8. When a push to `main` sets an item `done`, the mirror comments
   `Delivers #<issue> (<id>).` once on the pull request the commit subject
   names; a one-time backfill mode does the same for items already done.
   Pull-request bodies are never edited.
9. Each run reads the whole tree, compares, and writes only differences; a run
   with nothing changed writes nothing; a rerun on the same commit posts no
   second comment.
10. An issue without the marker is never touched.
11. An item file deleted from the tree: its issue is neither closed nor
    deleted, it is labelled `stale`, and the step summary warns. (The
    "neither closed" part is superseded by decision 0012: an open issue is
    closed as not planned.)
12. The workflow runs on a push to `main` touching `**/.issue/**`,
    `epics/**/epic.md` or the mirror's own files, and on manual dispatch; one
    run at a time, none cancelled; a step summary counts issues created,
    edited, closed, reopened, linked, commented, stale and skipped.
13. The workflow is generated by the NUKE build and committed, and uses the
    workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write` and
    `contents: read`, nothing else.
14. Writes are paced to stay under GitHub's secondary write limit; a run cut
    off part way is finished by the next run, by convergence.

## Why

Work in this repository is visible only to someone with a clone and the queue
script; a reader on GitHub sees one hand-filed issue and nothing of the
roadmap, what is done, or which pull request delivered what. A mirror shows
that on GitHub without moving the authority off the files that branches,
reviews and the queue script already read.

## Rejected

**Keep the work items with no GitHub presence.** Cost of rejecting: a workflow
with an `issues: write` token, a script to keep, and about 275 issues that say
they are a mirror. Taking it would cost the visibility the call above exists
for: the state of the work stays readable only from a clone.

**Migrate to GitHub issues and delete the work items.** Rejected the same day;
the reasons are decision 0002.

## Affects

- `0055-F9` § 1, § 3, § 4 C-1, C-2, C-3, § 5 rows 1 and 2.
- `0055-F8` A-2 and § 5 row 1, which now point here for the mirror.
- Epic `0055`, "Out of this epic".

## Reversal

None.
